intro_html: Takeout lo mein without the takeout markup: chewy noodles, tender chicken, and a glossy hoisin-soy sauce that clings to everything. Each bowl packs 57 grams of protein at 660 calories for about $4.31 (at everyday cost). The delivery apps want triple that before the fees even start.
cost_closing_html: About $4.31 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a full plate of chicken lo mein. The same order at a Chinese takeout spot runs $11 to $14 before tip and delivery fees, so this batch pays for itself by the second container.
shop_smart: Chicken breast in the big club pack costs about $2.23 a pound. The 6.25 pounds here is the priciest line at $13.77, and it is still cheaper than 2 pounds of restaurant chicken.
Regular wide egg noodles do the job of 'lo mein noodles' for a third of the price of anything labeled Asian noodles. Same wheat, same egg, different label.
Hoisin and oyster sauce look expensive per bottle, but they last across several batches. Counted at what this recipe actually uses, they add well under a dollar per bowl of restaurant-level flavor.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the sauce: hoisin, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, chicken broth, and cornstarch in a bowl until smooth. Set it by the stove.
Boil the egg noodles 1 minute short of the package time, drain, and toss with a little oil so they do not clump.
Slice the chicken breast into thin strips. Working in batches, sear in vegetable oil over high heat until cooked through to 165 F. Set aside.
In the same pot, stir fry the sliced red bell pepper 2 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, and most of the green onions for 1 minute more.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce, and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until it thickens and turns glossy.
Add the noodles and toss until every strand is coated. Finish with the remaining green onions.
Portion into 14 containers while still warm so the sauce distributes evenly.
portion_html: Set the full pot on the scale, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Weigh that amount into each container. Every bowl comes out to about 660 calories with 57 grams of protein.

steps: Whisk hoisin, soy, oyster sauce, sesame oil, broth, and cornstarch into a sauce.
Boil egg noodles just short of done and toss with a little oil.
Sear sliced chicken to 165 F, then stir fry pepper, garlic, ginger, and green onions.
Return chicken, add sauce, and simmer until glossy.
Toss in the noodles, coat well, and portion into 14 containers.
